spam.definition: A message is 'spam' if it is unsolicited, often sent in bulk, and typically promotes products, services, or scams; it may include misleading subject lines, excessive punctuation, or requests for personal information, distinguishing it from legitimate emails even when the topic appears similar.
examples: Get rich quick! Earn $5000 per week from home! No experience needed! Click here now!
URGENT: Your email account will be closed! Confirm your password immediately to avoid loss!

legitimate.definition: A 'legitimate' message is a solicited or expected communication, such as personal correspondence, work-related updates, or confirmed subscriptions, and does not attempt to deceive or push unwanted offers, even if occasionally promotional in nature.
examples: Hi John, just checking in about the project deadline next Monday. Are you on track?
Your monthly newsletter from The New York Times: here's what you missed this week.
